remarks: JMA is no longer empty. TC2630 is the first active system in the basin since Typhoon Saudel and Tropical Storm Krovanh dissipated, and the forecast track intensifies it to typhoon strength by roughly +69 hours. It is not a supply-chain event: the track runs north and then west-northwest through open water east of Japan, and the closest any forecast point comes to a tracked port is 1,188 km from Busan. Nothing enters the 600 km threat radius, so the system carries no threat rows and the incoming table stays empty.

Shanghai/Ningbo has been dropped from the port panel this run. Its eventEnded was set to 12 September two runs ago and the site's two-day window closed on 14 September, so the entry has aged out as intended rather than being renewed. The fishing-season channel closures that put it there are over.

Dropping that entry also lifts the suppression on the site's own 'berths idle' flag for Shanghai/Ningbo. That is deliberate. The queue there is still the largest on the board — 1.34m TEU and 223 ships at anchorage on the 13 September snapshot, with a queue-to-berth ratio of 2.14 — but that is congestion, not weather, and the congestion panel is the right place to read it.

No tracked port has a current closure, suspension or strike. The closures that do appear in this week's sources are at Dalian and Lianyungang, neither of which is on the tracked list, and both had resumed before the SEKO update went out.

All three per-port sources are stale rather than clean. SEKO has not moved since 11 September, Kuehne+Nagel has not published a 9-15 September edition at all, and MSC's newest items are commercial rather than operational. Read the absence of fresh closure reports as absence of evidence, not as confirmed normality.
